statement: Ella says: "My age now plus my age in 6 years makes 30." How old is Ella now?

choices.misconception: I divided 30 by 6 instead of thinking about two ages that add up to 30.
I halved 30 and then took 6 away, but the 6 years belong to only one of the two ages.
I halved 30, forgetting that her age in 6 years is 6 more than her age now.
I found how old Ella will be in 6 years instead of how old she is now.

hints: Her age in 6 years is her age now with 6 added.
Translate the sentence into a sum: two copies of Ella's age now, plus 6 extra years, make 30. Take away the extra part, then share what is left equally.
Take the 6 extra years away from 30. What is left is two equal ages.

solutions.reliable: Her age in 6 years is her age now plus 6. So the sentence says: age + age + 6 = 30. Take away the 6: two equal ages make 24, so one age is 24 / 2 = 12. Check: in 6 years she will be 18, and 12 + 18 = 30. The transferable idea: write the sentence as a sum, take away the extra part, then share equally.
solutions.elegant: The two ages are 6 apart and add up to 30, so they sit 3 either side of half of 30, which is 15. They are 12 and 18, and Ella is 12 now.

whyOnTest: Turning a sentence about two moments in time into one sum is the skill, and halving the total without removing the 6 is the tempting shortcut.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
